subject: SYDE

title: SYDE362 - Design Testing, Validation, and Verification
description: Engineering design project course where students work in small groups applying the principles of engineering problem solving and design, with a focus on testing and design evaluation, and an introduction to benchmark testing and applied design optimization. Student projects will provide hands-on experience with design verification, validation, and performance measurement and analysis using engineering tools.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE364 - Design Consultation
description: In this course, students will engage with stakeholders, colleagues, communities, and the natural world as they apply human-centered and participatory design practices to fully understand a complex design problem in its broader societal and environmental context. Students will develop and represent a deep understanding of the design problem while acknowledging their own knowledge gaps, deficiencies in existing solutions, and uncertainties. Students will work with each other and stakeholders to determine viable solution approaches while considering a wide range of options including new or changes to existing products, processes, infrastructure, policy, or other systems.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering

title: SYDE381 - Thermodynamics
description: An introductory course in engineering thermodynamics structured for students in systems design. Classical thermodynamics is presented as the systematic study of energy; its use, degradation, and waste. Introduction to heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation. Applications focus on problems of energy and environment. The concepts of statistical thermodynamics are introduced.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE382 - Multi-Physics Modelling and Simulation
description: Introduction to describing physical phenomena in differential form such as fluid flow (Navier-Stokes), thermodynamics (energy conservation, enthalpy, entropy), electro-magnetics (Maxwell equations), mechanics, and dynamics.  Topics include finite difference methods, finite element methods, boundary conditions, and iterative solvers.  The objective is to model with differential equations, predict what the result characteristics, solve models with FEM computational algorithms, and authenticate the results.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: MATH218, SYDE351; Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering students

title: SYDE383 - Fluid Mechanics
description: Fundamental concepts in systems involving fluid flow. Basic treatment of statics, kinematics and dynamics of fluids. Conservation of mass, momentum and energy for a control volume. Dimensional analysis and similarity. Flow in pipes and channels. Brief introduction to boundary layers, lift and drag, ideal and compressible flow.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3A Systems Design Engineering.

title: SYDE385 - Material Properties
description: An introduction to the properties, processing and structure of metals, semiconductors, polymers, ceramic, nanomaterials, and biomaterials. Introduction to mechanical response of materials and stress-strain relationships. Behaviour of prismatic members in tension, compression, shear, bending, and torsion. Shear-force and bending-moment diagrams and an introduction to instability.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3A Systems Design Engineering

title: SYDE400 - Work-Term Symposium Presentation
description: A work-term presentation is composed and presented at the Work-term Symposium. The presentation provides an opportunity for students to effectively communicate and reflect on their engineering experience gained during their co-op work terms. In the presentation, students draw connections between the theoretical aspects of engineering taught in the classroom and the practical applications of that theory in the workplace.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 4A Systems Design Engineering

title: SYDE401 - Seminar
description: Systems design fourth-year students will meet with a faculty member designated as their class professor. Conceptual difficulties, the interrelation of course work and engineering practice will be discussed.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE402 - Seminar
description: Systems design fourth-year students will meet with a faculty member designated as their class professor. Conceptual difficulties, the interrelation of course work and engineering practice will be discussed.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE411 - Optimization and Numerical Methods
description: Advanced methods for systems of linear equations. Root-finding methods. Linear programming, simplex and interior-point methods. Local and global optimization methods. Constrained optimization. Multiobjective and multidisciplinary design optimization.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering

title: SYDE461 - Systems Design Engineering Capstone Project 1
description: The first half of a two-term engineering design project continuing the systems design project sequence. Students work in small groups applying the principles of systems design engineering to a situation of concern of their own choosing. Students have individual project supervisors as well as an overall co-ordinator who provides the framework for the term assessments.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE462 - Systems Design Engineering Capstone Project 2
description: The second half of a two-term engineering design project continuing the systems design project sequence. Students work in small groups applying the principles of systems design engineering to a situation of concern of their own choosing. Students have individual project supervisors as well as an overall co-ordinator who provides the framework for the term assessments.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE499 - Elective Systems Design Research Project
description: A major undergraduate individual systems design engineering research project carried out as a technical elective (TE) under the supervision of a faculty member. Students are expected to demonstrate initiative and responsibility. An oral presentation of results and a written report are the minimum requirements. The faculty supervisor or department may set other requirements. Students will arrange for a faculty supervisor prior to registration.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE522 - Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
description: The objective of this course is to introduce students to fundamental concepts of artificial intelligence. An overview of different learning schemes will be provided, including supervised and unsupervised algorithms. The focus of this course will be on dimensionality reduction, clustering, classification, deep and shallow artificial neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Ethical aspects of artificial intelligence will be discussed.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: One of BME122, CS240/CS240E, ECE250, MSE240, MTE140, SYDE223 and Biomedical Engineering or SYDE or level at least 4A Management Engineering or Mechatronics Eng or Mechatronics Option or Computer Eng Option.

title: SYDE531 - Design Optimization Under Probabilistic Uncertainty
description: Optimization methods for real world problems have to deal with probabilistic uncertainty either due to data uncertainty or manufacturing uncertainty or both. Maximizing the expected value of the objective function subject to reliability (or risk) constraints is commonly used in such design or decision-making problems. Common methods used are stochastic programming, stochastic dynamic programming, chance-constraints, yield optimization and tolerance design. Example applications are selected from water management, energy systems, financial engineering, and manufacturing.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE532 - Introduction to Complex Systems
description: The overwhelming majority of societal, ecological and climate issues of pressing importance are complex systems; nonlinear dynamic interacting systems poorly characterized by linear analyses and Gaussian statistics. This course introduces the mathematics needed to understand such interactions, including nonlinear dynamics, critical and bifurcation behaviours, large-scale systems and power-law distributions. The mathematical methods will be motivated by extensive examples and case studies such as global warming, energy shortages, desertification, overpopulation, poverty, and economic instability, to be investigated from a systems engineering perspective that will connect mathematical concepts to real-world examples.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering or Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering

title: SYDE533 - Conflict Resolution
description: Formal methods for studying engineering decision-making problems involving multiple participants and multiple objectives. Topics include the graph model for conflict resolution, normal game form, metagame analysis, games with misperceptions, preference elicitation, human behaviour under conflict, evolution of a conflict, decision-making under uncertainty, sensitivity analyses, multiple criteria decision analysis, group decision and negotiation, coalition analysis, decision support systems, and real-world applications of the foregoing concepts.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE534 - Electric Energy Systems
description: Traditional electric energy systems comprising generation, transmission, and distribution are examined. Emerging technologies and trends are considered, such as competition, smart grids, energy storage, demand side management, renewable energy, and P2P. Future challenges and possibilities are then explored. Issues will be explored from technical, economic, environmental, sustainability, and social perspectives.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE535 - Computational Simulations for Societal and Environmental Systems
description: This course will introduce and apply the fundamentals of computational simulation for complex systems. Data collection and analysis, conceptual modelling, computational modelling, output analysis, and communication of results to non-expert audiences will be covered extensively. Students will develop computational simulations to explore potential solutions for complex societal problems, identifying emergent scenarios, costs, and benefits with the goal of informing decision-makers.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3A. Honours Software Engineering or BASc students only.
uwflow_antireqs: SYDE599, Topic 9, Computational Simulations for Societal & Environmental Systems

title: SYDE536 - Modelling Transportation Systems
description: Overview of frameworks used to model the global and community transportation systems followed by four case studies: Bayesian modelling of collision rates; discrete choice modelling of travel mode; operating mode-based time series modelling of tailpipe emissions, and simulation of traffic operations including congestion.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3A. Honours Software Engineering or BASc students.

title: SYDE537 - Artificial Life: Biology and Computation
description: Artificial life is the study of the simulation and synthesis of living or life-like systems. This course treats the basic principles of biology and computation in nature that underpin the organization of living systems in life as we know it, as it might exist elsewhere in the universe, and in digital or artificial media. We explore the mechanisms within living individuals that grow and change in a complex environment. This provides a variety of methods for understanding, modelling, and designing complex adaptive systems, whether naturally occurring or engineered, in simulation, in physical systems, with a view to applications in artificial life as the foundation for artificial intelligence and biological modelling.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE542 - Interface Design
description: This course focuses on the design of computer interfaces for simple to complex systems. Examples of applications are used to illustrate theoretical approaches. Main topics include forms of visual display; auditory display and soft controls; context, navigation, and layout; development techniques; design for engagement.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: One of BME162, MSE343, SYDE162, SYDE348/SYDE548, SYDE543; Biomedical Engineering or Systems Design Engineering or (level at least 4A Management Engineering or 4A Mechatronics Engineering) or Ergonomics and Injury Prevention Minor

title: SYDE543 - Cognitive Ergonomics
description: This course focuses on the role engineering psychology research plays in design of the information displays and devices associated with simple and complex cognitive tasks. Main topics include signal detection and target location tasks, navigation tasks, training tasks, communication tasks, human error, stress and mental workload, supervisory control, and situational awareness.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Biomedical Engineering or Systems Design Engineering or (Level at least 4A Mechatronics Engineering) or Biomechanics Option or Ergonomics and Injury Prevention Minor

title: SYDE544 - Biomedical Measurement and Signal Processing
description: This course develops an understanding of biomedical measurements through the examination of electromyographic (EMG), electroencephalographic (EEG), and electrocardiographic (ECG) signals. Measurement of human-body position, force, and pressure, and related instrumentation will also be presented. Signal processing techniques will be discussed in the context of extraction and application of useful biomedical signals.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: One of BIOL273, BME284, SYDE384/SYDE584; Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering or Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering or Level at least 3B Honours Life Physics (Biophysics Specialization)

title: SYDE548 - User Centred Design Methods
description: This course approaches the design of tasks, tools, products, and systems from a user-centered design perspective. Emphasis is on the human factors and usability methods, and techniques that can and should be applied throughout the iterative design process. While design issues pertaining to human-computer interaction are discussed, the methods presented can be applied to the design of almost any user interface. Major topics include user research methods for usability and user experience, inspection methods, user testing, applied statistical analysis.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: (Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering) or (Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering) or (Level at least 4A Mechatronics Engineering or Biomechanics Option or Ergonomics and Injury Prevention Minor).

title: SYDE552 - Computational Neuroscience
description: Introduction to modelling and analysis of neurophysiological systems. Models of synaptic plasticity and learning, with focus on the similarities and differences between neuroscience and deep learning.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering or Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering

title: SYDE553 - Advanced Dynamics
description: Newtonian and Eulerian formulation of particle and rigid body kinematics and dynamics. Energy (Lagrangian and Hamiltonian) formulations of particle and rigid body dynamics; generalized co-ordinates, generalized forces, holonomic constraints, Lagrange multipliers.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: (Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering) or (Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering) or (Level at least 4A Mechatronics Engineering) or Mechatronics Option or Biomechanics Option

title: SYDE554 - Nonlinear Dynamic Systems
description: This course introduces nonlinear systems with applications in realistic ecological, mechanical, electrical, and chemical engineering systems. The properties of those systems are investigated via analytical and numerical tools, with particular application to MEMS and NEMS actuators & sensors. Students will develop knowledge and appreciation of the following concepts and tools: differences between linear and nonlinear dynamic systems; autonomous and non-autonomous systems; existence and uniqueness of solutions; equilibrium points and limit cycles; phase plane analysis; nonlinear phenomena; Poincare section analysis; multi-frequency oscillations; notions of system stability (e.g., Lyapunov functions).
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE556 - Simulating Neurobiological Systems
description: This course develops and applies a general framework for understanding neural computation in the context of recent advances in theoretical and experimental neuroscience. Particular emphasis is placed on understanding representation, nonlinear computation, and dynamics in real neurobiological systems. Students will apply signal processing, control theory, linear algebra, probability theory, and similar quantitative tools for the purpose of modelling sensory, motor, and cognitive systems. Topics covered include single neuron function, neural coding, neural dynamics, attractor networks, learning, statistical inference, locomotion, working memory, etc. Familiarity with neural systems is helpful but not essential.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE572 - Introduction to Pattern Recognition
description: Pattern recognition as a process of data analysis. Pattern features as components in a random vector representation. Classification techniques; distance measures in feature space, probabilistic (Bayesian) decision theory, linear discriminants. Clustering and feature extraction. Applications; optical character recognition, speech recognition, industrial robot vision, medical diagnosis, remote sensing and satellite image analysis, fault detection and diagnosis in complex systems such as nuclear reactors.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: (Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering) or (Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering) or (Level at least 4A Mechatronics Engineering) or Mechatronics Option or Biomechanics Option

title: SYDE575 - Image Processing
description: Beginning with a discussion of quantitative models of imaging systems, this course moves on to apply methods of linear systems theory and signal processing to image processing. Simple spatial domain techniques as well as spatial frequency domain methods, and digital filter design for image enhancement and restoration are discussed. The key methods and problems are surveyed; edge detection, image denoising, image segmentation, image enhancement, image compression, image registration, and feature detection. Applications to machine vision, remote sensing, and medical imaging will be emphasized.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: BME252 or SYDE252; (Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering) or (Level at least 3B Systems Design Engineering) or (Level at least 4A Mechatronics Engineering) or Mechatronics Option or Biomechanics Option

title: SYDE577 - Deep Learning
description: Introduction to deep learning. Regression and classification; backpropagation; convolutional and recurrent networks; optimization and regularization of deep networks; transformers; recent developments in the field.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE584 - Physiological Systems and Biomedical Design
description: In this course, students will become familiar with the physiology and anatomical structures of the human body. The structure, functions, and properties of major physiological systems (e.g., musculoskeletal, nervous, cardiovascular, and respiratory) will be presented in relation to modelling physiological systems and the design of biomedical devices (imaging, assistive, and diagnostic). Various aspects of pathology and how they influence measurements will also be introduced.
subject: SYDE
uwflow_prereqs: (Level at least 3B Engineering) or (Level at least 3B Honours Life Physics (Biophysics specialization)).

title: SYDE586 - Material Selection for Design
description: Material selection based on material property and design requirements. Design a product and selected material against failure. Select a manufacturing process that meets design requirements and constraints. Incorporate economic analysis and environmental impact in the selection process. Assess life cycle of the product and the selected material. Case studies related to general engineering applications and biomedical applications.
subject: SYDE

title: SYDE599 - Special Topics in Systems Design Engineering
description: This course deals with selected topics at the undergraduate level in environmental and societal systems, mechatronics and physical systems, or human factors and ergonomics.
subject: SYDE

title: THPERF100 - Introduction to Theatre
description: A foundational studio course introducing students to the technical dimensions of theatre creation with emphasis on design and production processes. Students explore the material elements that bring performance to life through hands-on engagement with production technologies, design principles, and technical problem-solving. Through studio-based workshops and collaborative projects, students develop introductory skills in scenic construction, lighting, sound, costumes, and props while examining how these technical elements express genre, style, theme, and narrative structure. Students research and analyze influential dramatic works and develop original production designs that address contemporary issues such as race, gender, and sustainability. This required course establishes essential technical vocabulary, conceptual frameworks, and practical skills needed for both acting and production streams, with particular emphasis on how technical choices impact storytelling and audience experience.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF101 - Theatre and Performance Fundamentals
description: This foundational course introduces students to theatre through three integrated pillars: dramaturgy (historical context, critical investigation, theory), performance (acting techniques, creation, embodiment), and production and design (stagecraft and scenography). Designed for both theatre majors seeking essential foundations and students from all disciplines, the course develops critical thinking, artistic research practices, creative problem-solving, and collaborative abilities applicable across fields.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF102 - Introduction to Performance
description: A foundational studio course introducing students to the creative processes of performance across a range of contexts. Students develop core performance skills through embodied practice, collaborative creation, and critical reflection. The course emphasizes physical awareness, vocal expressivity, textual analysis, and ensemble building while exploring the relationship between performance and identity. Through progressive exercises, improvisation, scene work, and performance projects, students cultivate presence, authenticity, and creative risk-taking. This required course serves as the entry point to further specialization, establishing the groundwork for understanding performance as a mode of meaning-making and social engagement.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF112 - Introduction to Black Arts, Culture, and Literature
description: This course examines the evolution and development of Black Peoples' artistic, cultural, and literary experiences from a global perspective including art and design, theatre and performance, literature, music, spoken word, and other modes of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary practice. Coursework is designed to immerse students in analyzing Black art, culture, and literature through intersectional, feminist, and queer lenses. The course is designed for both thinkers and creators. Students will engage in the course material through readings, viewings, and field trips around film, comics, anime, popular culture events, plus the visual and performing arts.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF149 - Introduction to Critical Design Practices
description: How does design help us think? This studio course introduces students to practice-based methods for generating knowledge. Topics may include prototyping, performance as research, material thinking, multi-modal representation, and experience design. Students will test and explore how we learn differently through creative practices.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF220 - Performance Studies
description: This workshop course in performance studies explores performance as a way of knowing. It investigates performance as artistic practice and as a means of understanding historical, social, and cultural practices, including drama/theatre texts, poetry, narratives, and texts of everyday life.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF221 - Performing Text
description: Students explore techniques to analyze, interpret, and perform texts.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF222 - Intermediate Performance
description: Building upon foundations from THPERF100 and COMMST102/THPERF102, this studio course advances students' performance skills through increasingly challenging material and expanded creative exploration. Students deepen their physical and vocal expressivity while engaging with diverse acting approaches and performance styles that complexify their understanding of character development and textual interpretation. Through scene study, ensemble exercises, and collaborative projects, students cultivate artistic confidence and discover their individual creative voice. The course emphasizes the development of versatile performers who can navigate multiple performance contexts while beginning to identify their artistic interests and pathways toward advanced specialization.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF224 - Black Performance Studies
description: This course explores the genealogies and historical development of Black performance created in regions such as North America, the Caribbean, Africa, and Europe. Students will examine the influences of key artists and theorists. Students will be challenged to apply historical, political, and cultural contexts to the analysis of audio, text-based, and/or audio-visual materials. This course expands students' concepts of Black performance to include performative modes such as performance poetry, TV shows, music, and podcasts.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF233 - Staging Science: Embodying Knowledge Expression in the Sciences
description: This course explores the vital intersections between science and theatre, from the anatomical theatres of the 1700s to the rigour of laboratory experimentation to contemporary high-stakes science communication. Students develop practical, collaborative, and embodied performance skills while investigating how theatrical processes shape scientific knowledge production and public understanding. Object texts may include plays, genres of science writing, and performance theory. Through staging and assembling performances, students experiment with how media - materials, bodies, technologies, and spatial relationships - matter for making and expressing knowledge, ultimately cultivating dramaturgical approaches that bridge scientific and artistic modes of inquiry.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF239 - Introduction to Modern Arab and Muslim Drama
description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of modern Arab and Muslim drama, providing students with a deep understanding of its various contexts, genres, evolutions, themes, and aesthetic nuances. Moreover, students will actively engage in the transformative practice of Theatre of the Oppressed, where they will merge their creative skills with scholarly knowledge. Collaborating in groups, they will create and perform Forum plays that serve as reflections on pertinent socio-political issues explored in the course. This blend of theoretical exploration and practical application ensures a holistic and immersive learning experience, fostering critical thinking, empathy, and artistic expression.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF243 - Technical Production 1
description: This course offers Theatre and Performance students an opportunity to contribute as crew members on mainstage productions within the school, working within a specific technical area to realize the scenic, lighting, costume, sound, and projection elements that audiences will experience. Through extensive hands-on practice in wardrobe, carpentry, scenic painting, lighting, sound, and video projection, students integrate theoretical knowledge with the practical demands of live performance. The course requires a significant time commitment as students participate in design meetings, technical rehearsals, and fabrication sessions where they build and install elements for performance. All coursework is completed in person with minimal take-home assignments.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF244 - Technical Production 2
description: Building on THPERF243, this course deepens students' technical theatre skills through more advanced crew work on mainstage productions within the school. Students advance their practical expertise within their chosen technical area while taking on increased responsibility in the production process. Through ongoing participation in design meetings, technical rehearsals, and fabrication sessions, students refine their skills and develop greater independence in realizing performance elements. All coursework is completed in person with minimal take-home assignments.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF246 - Fundamentals of Design
description: This studio course provides a foundational introduction to the elements and processes of performance design. Students explore the fundamental principles of scenic, lighting, costume, sound, and projection design through hands-on projects and critical analysis. Emphasis is placed on developing visual literacy, understanding the elements of design and principles of composition, and learning scenographic thinking as a means of understanding performance creation across theatre, dance, opera, and performance art.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF248 - Project Management in the Arts
description: This course introduces students to principles of project management relevant in a broad range of contexts including theatre, dance, film, and digital media production. Students explore arts management concepts such as budgeting, communication, scheduling, leadership, problem-solving, and conflict resolution. Concepts are applied in case studies that accommodate individual student interests.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF271 - Performance History
description: This course offers a broad exploration of theatre and performance practices across time and cultures, examining the evolution of major genres, styles, and traditions with contextual emphasis on Western theatrical developments. From ancient rituals to contemporary expressions, students will investigate how diverse performance forms emerge from and respond to their historical, social, and cultural environments. The course balances the study of significant theatrical movements, texts, and artists with critical approaches to historical research and interpretation. By engaging with influential works and scholarly perspectives, students will develop a nuanced understanding of how performance has been created, documented, and reimagined throughout history, while considering the complex relationship between theatrical traditions and the societies that produce them.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF282 - Gender and Performance
description: This course explores how gender is performed on the stage and in the media. Key performances and performers are studied from the perspectives of critical feminist theory and performance studies. Students consider how performances can create, affirm, and disrupt how society understands and performs gender.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF290 - Special Topics in Theatre and Performance
description: Selected topics in theatre and performance at the introductory and intermediate level. Content varies based on faculty expertise, visiting artists, and student interest. Topics may include emerging trends in performance creation, specialized design techniques, contemporary theatre practices, theatre and performance studies, or interdisciplinary approaches to theatrical work.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF301 - Performance Creation
description: An integrated course exploring diverse approaches to creating original performance across multiple contexts and media. Students study, apply, and critique a range of collaborative creation methodologies, with special attention to site-specific performance and place-making through the body, language, space, and technology. The course emphasizes the relationship between creative processes and the significance of works in their communities, examining how performance can respond to, challenge, and transform social contexts. Through hands-on projects, students develop skills in collaborative leadership, interdisciplinary research, and critical analysis of artistic processes.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF306 - Production and Performance Practicum
description: This intermediate-level practicum course engages students in predominantly hands-on theatrical practice across performance, design, and production specializations through substantial leadership roles in the program's theatre productions. Building upon foundational coursework, students work alongside faculty, staff, and visiting artists to develop professional-level competencies in industry-standard practices. Across multiple practicum enrolments, students may explore different aspects of theatre creation, including performance, acting, directing, design, technical stagecraft, management, dramaturgy, and publicity, with each production offering distinct content and specialized focus areas that bridge academic learning with professional theatrical work.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF307 - Production and Performance Practicum
description: This intermediate-level practicum course engages students in predominantly hands-on theatrical practice across performance, design, and production specializations through substantial leadership roles in the program's theatre productions. Building upon foundational coursework, students work alongside faculty, staff, and visiting artists to develop professional-level competencies in industry-standard practices. description: This intermediate-level practicum course engages students in predominantly hands-on theatrical practice across performance, design, and production specializations through substantial leadership roles in the program's theatre productions. Building upon foundational coursework, students work alongside faculty, staff, and visiting artists to develop professional-level competencies in industry-standard practices. Across multiple practicum enrolments, students may explore different aspects of theatre creation, including performance, acting, directing, design, technical stagecraft, management, dramaturgy, and publicity, with each production offering distinct content and specialized focus areas that bridge academic learning with professional theatrical work.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF321 - Approaches to Acting with Text
description: Students apply conceptual and theoretical approaches to acting in traditions emphasizing the text as a resource for performance.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF322 - Advanced Performance
description: This intensive studio course challenges students with complex technique development and creative exploration through demanding classical and contemporary material. Students refine advanced physical and vocal skills while tackling challenging texts that require artistic maturity and technical precision. The course emphasizes integration of multiple performance approaches as students develop their distinctive artistic voice through advanced scene study, physical theatre techniques, and collaborative devising processes. Students push artistic boundaries through challenging solo and ensemble work that explores the full range of their developing abilities.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF326 - Performing the Voice
description: Students explore techniques to access and develop the voice as a resource for performance.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF343 - Stage Management
description: Students explore approaches to stage management for theatre and performance.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF346 - Intermediate Design
description: Building on design fundamentals, this intermediate studio course engages students in collaborative, project-based design practice. Students work independently and as a team to develop complete design concepts for theatre and performance works and integrated digital media projects that draw upon contemporary scenographic methods. The course emphasizes professional design processes, research methodologies, and the creation of design presentations for real-world production contexts. Students explore how design intersects with social issues and contemporary performance practices.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF361 - Approaches to Directing
description: Exploration of the director's task in its practical, theoretical, and historical aspects.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF364 - Shakespeare in Performance at the Stratford Festival
description: A historical, theoretical, and analytical introduction to Shakespeare's plays in performance, both on stage and screen, this course focuses on specific problems and decisive issues of past productions and of those in the current Stratford Festival season.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF366 - Writing for Performance
description: Students explore techniques for analyzing, interpreting, and creating texts for theatre and performance.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF367 - Voice and Text at the Stratford Festival
description: Taught by faculty and Stratford Festival coaches, this practical course invites students to explore acting techniques and exercises to develop their stage voice with a particular focus on Shakespeare's plays. This is a block course that meets in Stratford for two weeks in May, and may be taken with ENGL364/THPERF364, as the two courses are offered at complementary times.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF374 - Sustainability in Design
description: Students explore the interchange between performance design and sustainability. Emphasis will be placed on ecological and systems thinking as students engage with theoretical and practical projects throughout the term.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF376 - Political Performance
description: This course offers a practical and applied examination of how various forms of performance may bring about an experience of political conscientization because creating a performance can be considered a process of political enlightenment and engagement.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF377 - Indigenous Performance in Context
description: This course introduces students to the knowledge systems and performance history woven into the practices of First Peoples on Turtle Island and beyond. Through examination of performance genres ranging from Longhouse, Renewal, and Powwow ceremonies to Western theatre, pop music, and Wild West shows, students will gain understanding of the current Indigenous performance landscape through discussion and critique of design and production history as well as contemporary script analysis. This course engages students in Indigenous Ways of Knowing and helps them develop alternative approaches to research with particular attention to sustainable and holistic practices of performance making and design presentation. The class content will pay particular attention to traditions of the host nations (Haudenosaunee and Anishinaabe) when possible.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF378 - Race and Performance
description: This course explores how critical race and performance studies illuminate 20th- and 21st-century theatre and performance. Students investigate the historical, political, and cultural contexts that inform the creation and presentation of performance works involving race, examining how theatre-making can resist or perpetuate structures of oppression and colonization. Through embodied research practices and critical analysis, students explore how racial concepts find expression through performative communication and scenography. Applying intersectional and decolonial approaches, students develop skills to create equitable, accessible, and anti-oppressive performance experiences while building capacity to communicate effectively across diverse artistic contexts and navigate complex creative territories with care and self-awareness.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF379 - Mixed Reality Design
description: This course explores design for material-world experiences that incorporate virtual, augmented, and/or extended reality technologies. Emphasis is placed on the relationships among different modes of perception and how they affect our understanding of the real and the virtual.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF380 - Black Theatre in Practice
description: A workshop that explores the history, dramatic literature, and performance of Black theatre artists. Students will explore the relationship of Black theatre to artistic and public life. Special attention may be given to specific issues, periods, locations, and genealogies of Black theatre. Students will create performance pieces.
subject: THPERF
uwflow_prereqs: Level at least 2A or students pursuing the Diploma in Black Studies or the Diploma in Fundamentals of Anti-Racist Communication

title: THPERF386 - Shakespeare 1
description: A study of the plays written before 1599-1600, excluding Julius Caesar.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF387 - Shakespeare 2
description: A study of the plays written after 1599-1600, including Julius Caesar.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF390 - Advanced Special Topics in Theatre and Performance
description: Selected topics in theatre and performance at the advanced level. Topics may include emerging trends in performance creation, specialized design techniques, contemporary theatre practices, theatre and performance studies, or interdisciplinary approaches to theatrical work. Content varies based on faculty expertise, visiting artists, and student interest.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF400 - Advanced Production and Performance Practicum
description: This course serves as the culminating experience for Theatre and Performance majors. Students work at an advanced, independent level with faculty, staff, and visiting artists to create and reflect upon a major, collaborative performance project. As core members of the creative team, students engage in all areas of project creation, including research, conception, writing, direction, design, performance, production, stage management, production management, publicity, dramaturgy, critique, and documentation.
subject: THPERF
uwflow_prereqs: One of THPERF306, THPERF307, THPERF316, THPERF317; Theatre and Performance majors

title: THPERF406 - Production and Performance Practicum
description: This advanced-level practicum course engages students in predominantly hands-on theatrical practice across performance, design, and production specializations through substantial leadership roles in the program's theatre productions. Building upon intermediate practicum experience, students work alongside faculty, staff, and visiting artists to develop professional-level competencies in industry-standard practices. Across multiple practicum enrolments, students may explore different aspects of theatre creation, including performance, acting, directing, design, technical stagecraft, management, dramaturgy, and publicity, with each production offering distinct content and specialized focus areas that bridge academic learning with professional theatrical work.
subject: THPERF
uwflow_prereqs: One of THPERF306, THPERF307, THPERF316, THPERF317

title: THPERF440 - Performative Inquiry and Practice
description: This course explores how to create, perform, and analyze performance texts, here defined as including drama/theatre texts, poetry, narratives, and the texts of everyday life. Through readings and creative investigation, students will explore the links between the participant, the researcher, the site, and the impulse of inquiry.
subject: THPERF

description: Seminars in special areas of drama and theatre.
subject: THPERF

title: THPERF491 - Selected Seminars in Drama and Theatre Arts
description: Seminars in special areas of drama and theatre.
subject: THPERF

description: This course is designed to give the student an opportunity to complete a comprehensive presentation in their major area of concentration.

description: This course is designed to give the student an opportunity to complete a comprehensive presentation in their major area of concentration. Second part of THPERF/COMMST499A.

title: UCR191E - Communication in the Engineering Profession (AE, CIVE, ENVE, GEOE)
description: Designed for students in Architectural, Civil, Environmental, and Geological Engineering whose dominant language is not English, this course will enhance students' oral and written communication competencies in contexts relevant to the engineering profession.
subject: UCR
uwflow_prereqs: Architectural, Civil, Environmental, Geological Engineering students. Antireq COMMST191/ENGL191, GENE199 (Topic 2)

title: UCR192E - Communication in the Engineering Profession (COMPE, ELE, MGTE)
description: Designed for students in Computer, Electrical, and Management Engineering whose dominant language is not English, this course will enhance students' oral and written communication competencies in contexts relevant to the engineering profession.
subject: UCR

title: UNIV101 - Strategies and Skills for Academic Success
description: The goal for this course is to help students become successful independent learners. It takes a modelled approach to teaching learning strategies to students who struggle to meet the demands of a university curriculum. In the lectures, students will be taught various learning strategies that they will be able to apply to successfully meet the demands of their other courses. Students will then apply these modelled strategies in their other courses during a weekly application seminar. Students will be expected to demonstrate their understanding of the material through a variety of assignments.
subject: UNIV

title: VCULT100 - World Cinema and Visual Culture
description: Introduction to film analysis via national cinemas and their worldwide reception, taking into account the role of new technologies. This course acknowledges not only the importance of multiple languages and cultures on the planet today but also the rapidly growing international contexts, complicated chains of production and distribution, and vastly different cultures of spectatorship.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT101 - Art History and Visual Culture
description: This course takes a case study approach to examining the role of the art object as a means of communication within the history of visual culture. Particular attention will also be paid to the unique properties of a range of diverse media, both traditional and new.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT112 - Introduction to Black Arts, Culture, and Literature
description: This course examines the evolution and development of Black Peoples' artistic, cultural, and literary experiences from a global perspective including art and design, theatre and performance, literature, music, spoken word, and other modes of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary practice. Coursework is designed to immerse students in analyzing Black art, culture, and literature through intersectional, feminist, and queer lenses. The course is designed for both thinkers and creators. Students will engage in the course material through readings, viewings, and field trips around film, comics, anime, popular culture events, plus the visual and performing arts.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT200 - Visual Studies Across the Discipline
description: Weekly lectures by visiting faculty introduce students to how visual studies are conducted across and between the disciplines. Recognizing the vastness of the global study of visual culture, this course reinforces how, despite the diversity of media analyzed, various disciplines share related approaches and theories.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT201 - Global Histories of Art 1500-1800 C.E.
description: This course takes a survey approach to examining the role of the art object as a means of communication within the history of global visual culture. Students will study key examples of art, spanning the 16th to the 19th centuries, and will achieve a thematic comprehension of art’s role in shaping political structures, social mores, cultural discourses, and cosmological beliefs. Particular attention will also be paid to the unique properties of a range of diverse media, both traditional and new.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT204 - Art Institutions
description: This course examines the history of art institutions, such as museums, galleries, collections, artist run spaces, and considers their place and meaning in contemporary society. Students will explore the history and future shape of such institutions and examine current practices, issues, and debates surrounding them. Topics to be considered include the politics of the art institutions; history and discourse of collecting and display; history of curatorial practices and the development of exhibitions; art publics; technology and new media; collections and collecting practices; and issues  of artistic freedom and censorship.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT205 - Topics in Visual Culture
description: This course will cover different topics in visual culture. The content can change from term to term.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT208 - Global Modern Art: 1800-1940
description: A study of the global development of modern art (1800 to 1940). Topics such as primitivism, Impressionism, Cubism, Futurism, abstraction, imperialism, colonialism, artists' reactions to calamitous world events such as World War 1, and various methodologies, including semiotic and Marxist analyses, will be explored.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT209 - Global Modernisms: 1940-1970
description: This course introduces students to a thematically, materially, and geographically varied set of art practices which developed across the world from 1940-1970 and are referred to, under different monikers, as high modernism, mid-century modernism, and more recently global modernism. These variants of global art production are explored by analyzing theoretical and aesthetic ideas, as well as art movements and styles such as Socialist Realism, Gutai, Postcolonial Modernism, Cannibalist Aesthetic, Brutalism, Abstract Expressionism, Pop Art, Négritude, Indigenous Modernism, and others.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT216 - Indigenous Visual Culture in Canada
description: This course will introduce students to issues in contemporary Indigenous visual culture within the Canadian context. Special attention will be paid to the complexities of contemporary art and cultural practices. The course will examine both practice and relevant theoretical paradigms.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT241 - Survey of Greek Art and Architecture
description: A survey of Greek art and architecture from the earliest times to the coming of the Romans. Material studied may include the art of the Bronze Age, the development of Greek sculpture, the evolution of the Acropolis at Athens, and the change in art and architecture after Alexander the Great.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT242 - Survey of Roman Art and Architecture
description: A survey of Roman art and architecture from the earliest times to the age of Constantine the Great. Material studied may include the art of the Etruscans, the evolution of Roman portraiture, innovations in architectural materials and forms, the use of art and architecture by the Emperors, and the change to Late Antique art.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT244 - History of Visual Media to 1910
description: This course provides a chronological and thematic overview of the history of visual media examining technologies such as the printing press, photography, early cinema, and the representation of perspective.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT245 - History of Film and Visual Media from 1900 to Today
description: The course provides a chronological and thematic overview of the history of visual media in Modernity and Postmodernity. It starts at the beginning of the 20th century with the rise of cinema and ends with discussion of the digital age.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT252 - Religion in Popular Film
description: This course examines how religion has been a central concern and inspiration for filmmakers and how popular films have informed and shaped our understanding of religion.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT256 - Experimental Film
description: The course introduces students to the history, methodologies, theories, and aesthetics of non-narrative experimental film with a focus on intersections between film and visual and performing arts.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT257 - Video, New Media and the Digital Turn
description: This course analyzes the shift in visual practices of the 20th century transformed by the arrival of various digital technologies. An emphasis is placed on the increasing interdisciplinarity of new media, as well as their multi-sensory nature.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT262 - Global Queer Cinema
description: This course introduces the varied production of world-wide gay, lesbian, bisexual, and transgender cinema. Inquiry will focus on how queer cinematic production serves as a vehicle for documentation and education, aesthetic and sexual experimentation, as well as cultural export and self-inquiry.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT275 - Calligraphy to Conceptual Art: Text as an Image in Islamic and East Asian Visual Arts
description: Exploring the history of Islamic and East Asian calligraphic arts and the study of Eastern and Western artists, this course examines multiple ways in which writing and other forms of visible language are incorporated into visual arts. Through studio projects, students explore conceptual approaches to text-based image making.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT281 - Art and Gender
description: A study of selected themes dealing with gender in the history of art: e.g., the representation of the human body; portrayal of mythological, spiritual, and allegorical figures; professional and amateur artists and their status within societies; etc.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT282 - Canadian Art from the 17th Century to 1940
description: This course examines art in Canada from the beginning of the European settlement in the 17th century to the Group of Seven and the Canadian Group of Painters. Some of the issues that will be investigated include the perception of Canada from abroad, the "new world", nation and nationhood, and the invention and appropriation of culture.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT293 - Fine Arts Abroad
description: This is a topics course that provides students with an introduction to and a familiarity with the art and culture of a particular destination. Working in the field with landscape, cityscape, and monuments of art, students will employ a variety of media to develop techniques for visual reportage, documentation, note-taking, and journal-keeping. Individual aesthetic responses to a wide range of subject matter will be encouraged.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT300 - Visual Culture in Theory
description: An advanced introduction to theorizing in art and media, highlighting the distinctive role of visual representation in cultural experience and the varied modes of thinking about images that visual representation has engendered. Readings will be drawn from several disciplines including art history, film and literary studies, media studies, and philosophy.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT305 - Topics in Visual Culture
description: This course will cover different topics in visual culture. The content can change from term to term.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT319 - Contemporary Art
description: A survey of contemporary international art movements with emphasis on work since 1970. Readings in contemporary criticism and gallery visits are an integral part of the course.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT330 - Topics Course in Museums, Galleries, Curatorship
description: Often taught by the University of Waterloo Curator, this course explores a range of topics dealing with museums, galleries, and curatorial practices. Field visits may be a required component of this course.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT338 - Philosophy of Art
description: What is art? What is beauty? What do the two have to do with each other? This course introduces students to some fundamental issues in the philosophy of art, and to a variety of philosophical views on these issues.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT341 - Advanced Studies in Greek Art and Architecture
description: An advanced survey of the art and architecture from a selected time period of Greek history. Material studied may include the art and architecture of the Aegean Bronze Age, and the Archaic, Classical, and Hellenistic periods. Archaeological, historical, and cultural issues specific to each time period will be discussed through the important media of the day.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT342 - Advanced Studies in Roman Art and Architecture
description: An advanced survey of the art and architecture from a selected time period of Roman History. Material studied may include the art and architecture of the Etruscans, the Roman Republic, and the Roman Empire. Archaeological, historical, and cultural issues specific to each time period will be discussed through the important media of the day.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT377 - Religion in Science Fiction Films and Television
description: This course examines how religion, religious themes, and the religious imagination are explored in and through science fiction film and television. Topics include the use of science fiction to discuss questions of transcendence, humanity, and divinity, as well as the challenge of extraterrestrial and artificial lifeforms.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT393 - Fine Arts Abroad
description: This is a topics course that provides students with an introduction to and a familiarity with the arts and culture of a particular destination. Working in the field with landscape, cityscape, and monuments of art, students will employ a variety of media to develop techniques for visual reportage, documentation, note-taking, and journal-keeping. Individual aesthetic responses to a wide range of subject matter will be encouraged.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT400 - Visual Culture Seminar
description: This fourth-year honours seminar leads students through a variety of topics in the theory and history of visual culture. Through class discussions, readings, and presentations, students will engage in an interdisciplinary dialogue around what constitutes visual culture today and how to analyze it.
subject: VCULT
uwflow_prereqs: VCULT300; Level at least 3B Visual Culture Honours students.

title: VCULT401 - Advanced Visual Culture Seminar
description: This fourth-year level advanced visual culture seminar is designed to focus student research skills toward the development of a thesis project.
subject: VCULT

title: VCULT405 - Topics in Visual Culture
description: This course will cover different topics in visual culture. The content can change from term to term.
subject: VCULT

title: WKRPT100 - Work-term Report
description: A work-term report presenting in detail a technical project, activity, or analysis engaged by the student normally during the preceding work term. The report is evaluated on the basis of written communication skills and technical proficiency in the subject matter as demonstrated by the report. Work-term reports are required courses for the degree but their grades are not included in the average. However, failed work-term report evaluations may delay a student's progress as indicated in the Examinations and Promotions section of this calendar. Details regarding the evaluation of the work-term reports can be obtained from the student's program advisor.
subject: WKRPT
